experience.title: Chief Information Security Officer
experience.blurb: Leads Information Security and the Identity and Access Management group, protecting data integrity and operational resilience for 33,500 students and nearly 4,000 faculty across a global campus network. Uses AI tools built in house to reimagine how the security department works.

bullets.t: Led the GCC High research enclave, a segregated Microsoft 365 GCC High and Azure Government environment for Controlled Unclassified Information and export controlled (ITAR and EAR) data, through its CMMC Level 2 assessment, implementing all 110 NIST SP 800-171 controls and achieving a perfect score.

Built a unified dashboard that brings every Information Security and IAM application into one view, improving visibility across the environment and speeding the resolution of threats and vulnerabilities.

Created Reimagine IT to rethink how products and projects are developed and run across their whole life cycle: Frame it, Build it, Loop it, Launch it, Tend it. Teams plan and build together with AI as a partner, refine in short loops, and keep improving after launch, with security and IAM built in, not bolted on.

In less than three months, revamped and rearchitected the phishing and spam defense process, cutting the phishing and spam that reaches institutional email by 95% and reducing the time the team spends on it.

Mapped every tool, account lifecycle, and sign in path across the university and built a phased plan to move from repeated password prompts to signing in once, with Microsoft Entra ID as the front door and a live tracker for every step.

Lead enterprise cybersecurity strategy as an executive team member, aligning risk management, data protection, and threat mitigation with institutional goals.

caseStudies.title: Talon Secure: A Perfect CMMC Level 2 Score
caseStudies.challenge: Researchers needed a place to store and work with Controlled Unclassified Information and export controlled (ITAR and EAR) data for DoD, DoE, and other federal research that would stand up to CMMC requirements.
caseStudies.approach: Led the GCC High research enclave with partner Planet Technologies: a segregated environment on Microsoft 365 GCC High and Azure Government with approved collaboration tools, protected storage, virtual desktops, and controlled communication. Translated NIST SP 800-171 into daily practice, leading the implementation of all 110 required controls across 14 families, from access control and audit logging to incident response and configuration management. Drove the documentation, policies, control validation, mock assessments, and evidence needed for a C3PAO assessment.
caseStudies.why: CMMC, the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification, is how the Department of War, formerly the Department of Defense, verifies that the contractors and research partners it works with protect Controlled Unclassified Information. Level 2 requires every one of the 110 security requirements in NIST SP 800-171, checked by an independent assessor against 320 objectives. Without it, a university is shut out of a growing share of defense research. A perfect score shows the controls work in practice, not just on paper.
caseStudies.result: A perfect score from a Certified Third Party Assessor Organization: 110 security controls tested against 320 assessment objectives, with no deficiencies in any of the 14 security categories. Faculty can now pursue larger Department of War grants and partner with defense companies.

quote.text: The assessment confirmed our protections are followed in practice, not just written down.
quote.by: Nic Carroll, quoted by Georgia Southern University

caseStudies.credit: The university's Research Security and Export Controls director credited Nic and his team with taking point on preparation.

caseStudies.title: Rearchitected Email Defense: 95% Less Phishing and Spam
caseStudies.challenge: Phishing and spam were getting through to institutional email, putting students, faculty, and staff at risk and taking up a large share of the security team's time.
caseStudies.approach: Revamped the phishing and spam defense process from the ground up and rearchitected how email threats are filtered, handled, and resolved, all in less than three months.
caseStudies.result: A 95% reduction in phishing and spam reaching institutional email services, and far less time spent by the team handling it.
caseStudies.metricLabel: Less phishing and spam reaching inboxes

caseStudies.title: Reimagined Third Party Review: 4,000+ Products in Six Months
caseStudies.challenge: Departments, divisions, and researchers needed new software, hardware, and extensions approved, but the review process was hard to see into and legal, procurement, and IT each worked on their own.
caseStudies.approach: In my first six months, completely changed the third party review and approval process. Made it transparent to requesters and built legal review, procurement, and information technology systems review into a single path, strengthening vendor risk management and data privacy.
caseStudies.result: More than 4,000 products reviewed and approved, from Chrome extensions, hardware, and applications for the research environment to the tools departments and divisions use every day.

caseStudies.title: Policy Library: Every Policy, From Need to Next Review
caseStudies.challenge: Policies, standards, and procedures were spread across published collections, with no single view of which were current, which were overdue for review, or where Georgia Southern's policies agreed or conflicted with the University System of Georgia manuals.
caseStudies.approach: Built the Policy Library and a complete process that takes a need to an approved SOP, policy, and procedure in eight steps. A leadership dashboard shows policy health by area, review schedules, revisions in progress, and decisions waiting on leadership. Revisions open the policy as the document itself, with tracked changes, paragraph comments, reviewer verdicts, and Cabinet and President sign offs. Every policy is compared sentence by sentence against the USG manuals, and people can ask questions in plain words and get answers cited to the official text.
caseStudies.result: One place to find, revise, approve, and track every policy. Leadership sees what is overdue and what needs a decision, policies that only restate USG are flagged to retire, possible conflicts are flagged for revision, and every edit, comment, and sign off is logged for audits and open records requests.
caseStudies.metricLabel: From draft to posted policy and its next review

caseStudies.title: Reimagine IT: Rethinking How Products and Projects Are Built
caseStudies.challenge: Projects followed the old way: scope for weeks, build behind closed doors, deliver once, and hope it fits. Every change pulled the whole team back together, and staff were tied to old habits, processes, and tools.
caseStudies.approach: Tasked by the CIO with rethinking how the university builds tools, I designed Reimagine IT, a five move cycle: Frame it, Build it, Loop it, Launch it, Tend it. The project owner builds with university approved AI tools while security, IAM, applications, UX, and academic partners shape the work in the room. Guardrails are set once, up front, and every project has one named owner, a backup, and a shared record from the first hour to the change catalog.
caseStudies.result: A new life cycle for any product or project, an app, a process, or anything else. Teams frame the end game, plan and build together with AI as a partner, refine in short loops, launch to a test group or to everyone, and keep improving after launch.

caseStudies.title: Sign In Once: Reimagining Single Sign On and Authorization
caseStudies.challenge: Students, faculty, and staff were asked to sign in again and again. Three different systems checked passwords behind about ten sign in services, and settings no one had chosen added prompts. Students, who mostly use their own laptops and phones, felt it most.
caseStudies.approach: Mapped the whole sign in experience end to end: every tool and the sign in it uses, how accounts are created and removed, and a day of sign ins for each kind of user. Built a phased plan to make Microsoft Entra ID the single front door with the existing campus sign in kept behind it, a separate track for personal devices, quick wins the teams could ship without buying anything, and a live tracker so every step's status is visible to everyone involved.
caseStudies.result: A clear path from two or three password prompts each morning to signing in once: none on a university computer and one on a personal device, with every sign in logged and protected by the same MFA rules in one place.
caseStudies.metricLabel: Instead of 2 to 3 prompts each morning

caseStudies.title: A National Data Privacy and Security Agreement for Education
caseStudies.challenge: Every district and university negotiated data privacy and security terms with every edtech supplier on its own, slowing procurement and leaving protections for student data uneven from one contract to the next.
caseStudies.approach: Served as an institutional representative on the 1EdTech task force of 33 K12, state education, and edtech supplier experts that created the Data Privacy and Security Agreement (DPSA) Template, a single agreement that covers both data privacy and data security. Helped shape the terms institutions and suppliers now use to protect student data, mitigate security risks, and speed up RFPs and contracting.
caseStudies.result: A national DPSA Template available to every 1EdTech member institution and supplier, part of the 1EdTech TrustEd Apps Program and adopted by districts such as Prince George's County Public Schools. Recognized with a 1EdTech Leadership Award at Learning Impact 2024, and invited to present the DPSA to members in a 1EdTech webinar.

quote.text: The 1EdTech Data Privacy and Security Agreement empowers K-12 school members by streamlining access to educational resources, fostering collaboration, and enhancing data privacy and security between vendors and institutions, reducing onboarding time and ultimately enriching the learning experience for all.

caseStudies.title: RosterEditor: Fix OneRoster Files Without the Wait
caseStudies.challenge: Districts often need to combine sections, swap teachers, or correct a roster before it reaches ClassLink, and that work usually means waiting on the student information system or hand editing CSV files.
caseStudies.approach: Built RosterEditor, which imports a OneRoster 1.1 or 1.2 bulk file and lets staff combine sections and courses, add or swap teachers, and fix any row in a dashboard or through a REST API, then exports a clean file in the same version for ClassLink. The combining rules are built in, so no AI is needed to do the work.
caseStudies.result: A live demo with invented data built on real Georgia state course codes, preview before every change, undo for the last 50 edits, and the first step toward an open source rostering hub.
caseStudies.blurb: Edit OneRoster 1.1 and 1.2 rosters for ClassLink: combine sections and courses, add or swap teachers, and export a clean file. Rules are built in, no AI required.

caseStudies.title: EduSite: One Accessible Platform for Every District and School Site
caseStudies.challenge: Districts must meet the ADA Title II rule (WCAG 2.1 Level AA) on the district site and every school site, often with separate tools, inconsistent menus, and high costs.
caseStudies.approach: Built EduSite, one install that runs the district site and every school site from a single dashboard, with shared menus and theme, drafts, review, and an audit log, accessibility checks that block publishing on errors, and an AI assistant where staff type or dictate changes without breaking the design.
caseStudies.result: A live beta demo modeled on Columbia County and Aiken County with a district switcher, built to stay low cost for districts to run themselves or have hosted.
caseStudies.blurb: One accessible platform that runs a district site and every school site from a single dashboard, with an AI assistant for staff updates.

agents.group: Agents That Work on a Schedule
agents.intro: Each one runs by itself, checks its own work with tests, and hands me a pull request to review. None of them can release anything without my approval.

items.name: Daily Security Engineer
items.text: Patches dependencies, reviews the day's changes, and probes one deeper area each weekday, from sign in to data exposure.

items.name: Daily Improvement Engineer
items.text: Ships one finished, tested improvement a night, rotating between bugs, design, state reporting, and speed.

items.name: Directions Writer
items.text: Keeps step by step directions current for every tool and every user group, verified against the running app.

items.name: Walkthrough Deck Keeper
items.text: Updates the walkthrough slides and screenshots whenever a feature changes.

items.name: Cost Keeper
items.text: Rechecks cloud list prices and recalculates the hosting cost for small, medium, and large districts.

items.name: Project Manager
items.text: Runs last, tracks every bug and change, checks that each agent ran, and writes my morning brief.

items.name: Infrastructure Engineer
items.text: Reviews hosting, sizing, and cost, and runs one cloud load test a month to prove capacity before busy seasons.

items.name: Daily Improvement Engineer
items.text: Reviews the app through six personas, picks the best value fix, builds it with tests, and opens one pull request.

items.name: Persona Tester
items.text: Uses each product as a different invented person every day and fixes the most useful thing it finds.

items.name: Security Reviewer
items.text: A read only review of recent changes and scan results across every repository, reported by severity.

items.name: Data Update Checker
items.text: Checks the state's public data downloads for new files and records what changed.

agents.intro: Reusable specialists I wrote as agent definition files. I call one in when a change touches its area.

items.name: Accessibility Auditor
items.text: Audits pages for WCAG 2.2 AA in light and dark mode, on desktop and phone, and fixes failures.

items.name: Design Reviewer
items.text: Reviews layout against Material Design 3 and the project style, then fixes what it finds.

items.name: Dashboard Designer
items.text: Designs charts and dashboards so every number is clear and opens the records behind it.

items.name: UX Writer
items.text: Rewrites page text, labels, and error messages so staff and families understand them at a glance.

items.name: Infrastructure Engineer
items.text: The full role definition behind the monthly hosting and capacity review.

items.name: Code Reviewer
items.text: An unbiased reviewer with no prior context, focused on security boundaries, correctness, and performance.

items.name: QA Agent
items.text: Writes and runs adversarial tests for correctness, boundary safety, and error handling.

items.name: Deep Research Agent
items.text: Investigates technical and security questions across the web and the codebase.

agents.intro: Read these first. The front door agent takes any IT request and routes it to the right department.

items.name: Start Here
items.text: What the set is, how the core IT set and the three sector packs fit together, how to load an agent into any AI tool, and how the agents hand work to each other.

items.name: Agent Roster
items.text: Every agent and skill in the set, with each agent's mission and the agents it calls on.

items.name: IT Front Door Agent
items.text: The single starting point for any request. Sends it to the right category or sector lead and coordinates work that crosses them.

agents.intro: The chief roles and the leaders who set direction, budget, and priorities.

items.name: Executive Leadership Lead Agent
items.text: Takes requests about strategy, budget, governance, and leadership decisions, sends each to the right role agent, and coordinates work that needs more than one.

items.name: Chief Information Officer (CIO)
items.text: Make technology advance the institution's goals, with a budget, team, and portfolio that leadership can trust.

items.name: Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
items.text: Give the institution a technology foundation that is reliable, secure, affordable, and ready for what comes next.

items.name: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
items.text: Protect the institution's people, data, and operations by running a security program matched to its real risks.

items.name: Chief Data Officer (CDO)
items.text: Make the institution's data trusted, well governed, and used for better decisions.

items.name: Chief AI Officer
items.text: Help the institution use AI to improve work and learning in ways that are safe, fair, and worth the cost.

items.name: Chief Digital Officer
items.text: Make the institution's services simple to find and use on any device.

items.name: Deputy or Associate CIO
items.text: Run IT day to day so the CIO's strategy is delivered on time and on budget.

items.name: Vice President of IT
items.text: Lead multiple IT divisions so they act as one organization with shared goals and wise use of money.

items.name: IT Director, Executive Director, IT Manager
items.text: Lead a team or functional area so it delivers reliable service and its people grow.

agents.intro: The people users reach first: help desk, desktop, field, and training support.

items.name: Service Desk and End User Support Lead Agent

items.name: Help Desk Technician (Tier 1, 2, 3)
items.text: Get people back to work quickly and leave a record that helps prevent the next problem.

items.name: Desktop Support Specialist

items.name: Field Technician

items.name: Service Desk Manager
items.text: Run a service desk that answers quickly, resolves well, and learns from every ticket.

items.name: Endpoint or Client Systems Administrator
items.text: Keep every managed device configured, patched, and secure with as little hands on work as possible.

items.name: Audiovisual and Classroom Technology Specialist

items.name: IT Asset Manager
items.text: Know what hardware and software the institution owns, where it is, who has it, and what it costs.

items.name: IT Trainer
items.text: Help people use the institution's technology with confidence, so they need less support.

items.name: Wireless Engineer

items.name: Cloud Engineer

items.name: Storage and Backup Administrator

items.name: Telecommunications or Voice Engineer

items.name: Network Operations Center (NOC) Technician

items.name: Infrastructure Manager
items.text: Lead the infrastructure teams so services stay reliable and the platform keeps up with need.

agents.intro: Security operations, engineering, risk, response, and awareness.

items.name: Cybersecurity Lead Agent
items.text: Takes requests about threats, incidents, vulnerabilities, risk, and security design, sends each to the right role agent, and coordinates work that needs more than one.

items.name: Security Analyst, SOC Analyst
items.text: Detect, investigate, and escalate suspicious activity quickly and accurately so real threats are contained early and noise does not bury them.

items.name: Security Engineer
items.text: Build, tune, and maintain the security tooling and detections the team depends on, and remove toil from the people who use them.

items.name: Security Architect
items.text: Make sure security is designed into systems and projects from the start, with clear standards that teams can follow without asking permission each time.

items.name: Incident Responder
items.text: Contain, eradicate, and recover from security incidents with the least harm, and make sure each incident leaves the organization stronger.

items.name: Threat Hunter, Threat Intelligence Analyst
items.text: Find threats the automated tools missed and turn outside intelligence into detections and decisions the team can use.

items.name: Penetration Tester, Red Team Operator
items.text: Find exploitable weaknesses before real attackers do, and give owners findings they can reproduce and fix.

items.name: Vulnerability Management Analyst
items.text: Keep the organization's exposure low by finding vulnerabilities, ranking them by real risk, and driving them to closure.

items.name: Digital Forensics Examiner
items.text: Collect and analyze digital evidence in a way that is accurate, repeatable, and defensible.

items.name: Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) Analyst
items.text: Give leadership an accurate picture of risk and compliance, and make meeting requirements as light as possible for the teams doing the work.

items.name: Security Awareness Coordinator
items.text: Help every person in the organization recognize and report threats, and prove that behavior is improving.

items.name: Application Security Engineer
items.text: Reduce security defects in the software the organization builds and buys by building security into the development process.

items.name: Cloud Security Engineer
items.text: Keep cloud environments secure by default through guardrails, continuous posture monitoring, and fast correction of drift.

items.name: SOC Manager
items.text: Run a SOC that detects and responds reliably every day, with a team that is trained, staffed, and getting better.

items.name: Deputy CISO
items.text: Run the security program day to day so it delivers on strategy, on budget, and with a clear line of sight from work to risk reduced.

agents.intro: Accounts, sign in, access reviews, and privileged access.

items.name: IAM Analyst
items.text: Make sure the right people have the right access at the right time, and that access is removed when it is no longer needed.

items.name: IAM Engineer
items.text: Build and run the systems that create, change, and remove accounts and that sign people in securely and simply.

items.name: IAM Architect
items.text: Define the identity model, standards, and roadmap that let every system trust who a person is and what they should reach.

items.name: Director of IAM
items.text: Lead the IAM program so that access is secure, fast, and well governed, with a team that has clear scope and priorities.

items.name: Privileged Access Management (PAM) Administrator
items.text: Protect the most powerful accounts by vaulting credentials, limiting standing privilege, and keeping a record of privileged use.

items.name: UX/UI Designer

items.name: Engineering Manager

agents.intro: How agents hand work to each other and make the work better over time.

items.name: Process Improvement Review
items.text: Use when a task is slow, error prone, or done differently each time and you want a better way to do it.

items.name: Efficiency Audit
items.text: Use when you want to find where time, money, or effort is being spent without a matching result.

items.name: Effectiveness Scorecard
items.text: Use when you need to show whether the work is achieving its purpose, not just getting done.

items.name: Agent Handoff
items.text: Use every time one agent asks another agent for help or passes work on.

items.name: Automation Finder
items.text: Use when a task or a handoff repeats and you want to know whether to automate it.

items.name: After Action Review
items.text: Use after any incident, project, exercise, or task that did not go as planned, or that went unusually well.
